model_claims.text: get_latex_string() now escapes LaTeX special characters (&, _, %, #, $, \, {, }, ~, ^) in cell and header strings.
model_claims.source_quote: Escape LaTeX special characters in get_latex_string()

model_claims.text: Previously, get_latex_string() wrote raw cell and header strings directly into the LaTeX tabular environment without escaping characters that have syntactic meaning in LaTeX, causing tables containing these characters to fail to compile.
model_claims.source_quote: `get_latex_string()` was writing raw cell and header strings directly into the LaTeX tabular environment without escaping characters that have syntactic meaning in LaTeX (`&`, `_`, `%`, `#`, `$`, `\`, `{`, `}`, `~`, `^`). Because of this, tables containing these characters would fail to compile (e.g. `&` creating extra alignment columns or `%` commenting out the rest of the line and row terminators).

model_claims.text: The _escape_latex helper escapes special characters using a single-pass regex replacement.
model_claims.source_quote: Added `_escape_latex` helper to escape special characters using single-pass regex replacement.

model_claims.text: Field names and cell data are escaped in _get_simple_latex_string() and _get_formatted_latex_string() when escape_header and escape_data options are True.
model_claims.source_quote: Escaped field names and cell data in `_get_simple_latex_string()` and `_get_formatted_latex_string()` when `escape_header` and `escape_data` options are True (which preserves the existing default behavior).

model_claims.text: A regression test test_latex_special_characters_escaping was added in tests/test_prettytable.py.
